speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. Have these symptoms been present for a few weeks, and do you notice any muscle weakness in your legs or trouble chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very concerning; do you experience significant fatigue during daily tasks like brushing your teeth or lifting objects? Also, have you noticed any changes in your speech, swallowing, or drooping eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase (CK), Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies, and Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
